title: Cyril of Jerusalem on Exodus 2:8
body: “Cyril's argument is fully justified by the actual usage of "Almah," which certainly refers to unmarried women in Gen.”
author: Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 2:15
body: “When the "intercession" of Moses is spoken of, it is natural to suppose that the reference is to Exod.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 3:8
body: “What again is "spiritual blessing in the heavenly places?" It is not upon earth, he means, as was the case with the Jews.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 12:4
body: “Again, shouldest thou ask the Jew why he expels all leaven from all his borders; here he will even be silent and will not so much as state any reason. And this is because, although some indeed of the circumstances were both types of things to come, and also due to things then happening; yet others were not so, that the Jews might not deal deceitfully; that they might not abide in the shadow.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 17:4
body: “Next, tell me with what view were they to take such a course? They did not immediately, leaving Judæa, go into the Gentile cities, but went up and down within its limit.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 19:10
body: “Well: I know that a chill comes over you (narkate) on hearing these things; but what am I to do? For this is God's own command, continually to sound these things in your ears, where He says, "Charge this people; (Fors.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 20:21
body: “At first sight it looks as if this sentence were out of place here. But the connection may be thus explained: this circumstance, of the cloud, is not idle, but very significant; and the minds of the disciples were alive to its import, as betokening His Godhead.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on Exodus 32:11
body: “When the "intercession" of Moses is spoken of, it is natural to suppose that the reference is to Exod.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans
